newsitem.title: FRANCE: France checks Sobhraj's nationality, past.
newsitem.headline: France checks Sobhraj's nationality, past.

text.p: France said on Tuesday it was checking the nationality and past activities of convicted killer Charles Sobhraj, moves which are delaying his awaited expulsion from India.
"This is an extremely serious criminal case and we are therefore compelled to verify his identity, nationality and legal procedures," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
India on Monday ordered the deportation of Sobhraj to France, as he is presumed to be a French citizen, and barred him from re-entering the country again.
Sobhraj's lawyer told reporters in New Delhi on Monday it was likely his client would be expelled later the same day with travel documents supplied from the French embassy.
But in Paris, the Foreign Ministry said the travel documents had not yet been given to Saigon-born Sobhraj pending checks on the authenticity of his French nationality.
Foreign Ministry officials could not say how long the checks would last.

Justice Ministry officials also said they were checking whether there were possible legal claims against Sobhraj in France. He was last in France nearly 30 years ago when he escaped from a prison near the Franco-German border and headed for Asia.

Sobhraj, 52, was first arrested in India for holding up a hotel jewellery shop in 1971. He has since been charged with a long string of crimes including murders of young back-packing foreign tourists.

Sobhraj has expressed plans to concentrate on working on a $15 million English-language film based on his life, to be produced in France with American actors. He said he would write the script but would not play the title role.
A parliamentary deputy called on the government to ensure Sobhraj be prevented from making any money in France from his past activities.
